lesson.title: Where Do I Start? A Math and Reading Placement Check
lesson.topic: A short, friendly placement quiz in math and reading shows where each learner should start, so lessons are not too easy or too hard.
lesson.steelman: Is it fair to start everyone at their grade level, or should each learner start where their skills actually are?
lesson.steelman_for: Starting at the right level avoids boredom and frustration, and lets a learner move fast through what they already know.
lesson.steelman_against: A single quiz on a single day can be wrong (nerves, a bad night's sleep), so a placement should be a starting guess, not a label.
lesson.example: Imagine Jonah, 8, who reads chapter books easily but freezes on subtraction with borrowing. His placement check starts him on harder reading and on two-digit subtraction, and he moves up in a week.
lesson.activity: With a grown-up, do a 15-minute check: read one short passage aloud and answer three questions, then try ten math problems that get harder. Stop when three in a row feel hard. Write down your starting point for each.
check_questions: Why do a placement check before starting lessons?
What should happen if the check seems wrong after a week?
What was your starting point in math and in reading?
